info.name: Egoola API — Seller App (seller-facing APIs)
info.description:
The APIs built for sellers: public location lookups, sign-up with KYC documents, seller login, the seller's own profile (/seller/me), resubmit after a rejection, change password, **product listings and gigs** (and their thumbnails). Read docs/seller/seller-api-guide.md (sections 6, 6b, 6.8) and docs/listing-complete-guide.md (sections 14, 15) alongside it.

Run top to bottom. Requests named **[Admin step]** are NOT seller APIs: they play the admin (approve, reject, suspend, clean up) so you can see what a seller experiences after each decision. The admin APIs themselves are in Egoola-Seller.postman_collection.json.

Requests with file rows need a real JPG / PNG / WEBP / PDF chosen in the Postman app (file paths cannot be shared in a collection).

exec: // A fresh value for every request, so emails and phones never repeat (the built-in {{$timestamp}} only changes once a second).

item.name: Setup — admin login (only for the [Admin step] requests)

request.description: Public endpoint — no token needed. Returns access + refresh JWTs carrying actor_type=admin. Every Seller Management endpoint below is Admin-only.
Exchanges the saved refresh token (14-day life) for a new access token (1-hour life). Run this instead of logging in again once the access token expires.
Public, read-only, no token. Fills the country dropdown on the sign-up form. Rows: id, name, slug, country_code, flag_url.

exec: pm.test("has countries", () => { const r = pm.response.json().results; pm.expect(r.length).to.be.at.least(1); pm.expect(r[0]).to.have.all.keys('id','name','slug','country_code','flag_url'); });

request.description: Call again whenever the country changes. Rows: id, name, slug, country.

exec: pm.test("every state belongs to the country", () => { pm.response.json().results.forEach(r => pm.expect(String(r.country)).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('country_id'))); });

request.description: Filters: `country`, `state`. Rows: id, name, slug, country, state.

exec: pm.test("every city belongs to the state", () => { pm.response.json().results.forEach(r => pm.expect(String(r.state)).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('lookup_state_id'))); });

item.name: Thanas of the chosen city (dropdown 4, optional)

request.description: Filters: `country`, `state`, `city`. The thana is optional on the sign-up form, so an empty list is normal.
`search` matches part of the name. Every list also takes `limit` (default 500, max 1000) and `offset`.

item.name: A stale token does not break a public read

request.description: Public routes ignore the Authorization header, so an expired token in the browser can never cause a 401 here.
Creating, editing and deleting geography stays on the admin API (`/api/v1/geography/`).

Public — no token. Multipart form. The seller is created unverified and inactive and joins the admin's Seller Request queue. **Pick a JPG, PNG, WEBP or PDF file for each `media_file` row in the Postman app** — a shared collection can't carry file paths, so under Newman these file rows are empty and the request fails with 400.

exec: pm.test("password and tokens are not returned", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b).to.not.have.property('password'); pm.expect(b).to.not.have.property('access'); });

item.name: Register Seller — with business profile, certificate and photo

request.description: Same endpoint with the optional parts: more documents (`media_for` + `media_file` pairs, same order), a profile photo, and the business profile as a JSON string in `info` (every business field is required when `info` is sent). **Pick a JPG, PNG, WEBP or PDF file for each `media_file` row in the Postman app** — a shared collection can't carry file paths, so under Newman these file rows are empty and the request fails with 400.

exec: pm.test("still unverified and inactive", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.verification_status).to.eql('unverified'); pm.expect(b.status).to.eql('inactive'); });

request.description: At least one NID file is required.

exec: pm.test("names the missing documents", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.media_for || b.media_file).to.exist; });

item.name: Register Seller — certificate but no NID (expect 400)

request.description: A certificate does not replace the NID. **Pick a JPG, PNG, WEBP or PDF file for each `media_file` row in the Postman app** — a shared collection can't carry file paths, so under Newman these file rows are empty and the request fails with 400.

Run after the first registration. The check ignores upper/lower case. **Pick a JPG, PNG, WEBP or PDF file for each `media_file` row in the Postman app** — a shared collection can't carry file paths, so under Newman these file rows are empty and the request fails with 400.

Run after the first registration. **Pick a JPG, PNG, WEBP or PDF file for each `media_file` row in the Postman app** — a shared collection can't carry file paths, so under Newman these file rows are empty and the request fails with 400.

The password must pass the project's password rules (8+ characters, not common, not all digits). **Pick a JPG, PNG, WEBP or PDF file for each `media_file` row in the Postman app** — a shared collection can't carry file paths, so under Newman these file rows are empty and the request fails with 400.

item.name: Register Seller — city from another state (expect 400)

request.description: State, city (and thana) must belong together. **Pick a JPG, PNG, WEBP or PDF file for each `media_file` row in the Postman app** — a shared collection can't carry file paths, so under Newman these file rows are empty and the request fails with 400.

item.name: Register Seller — missing address and location (expect 400)

request.description: Both addresses and country, state and city are required. **Pick a JPG, PNG, WEBP or PDF file for each `media_file` row in the Postman app** — a shared collection can't carry file paths, so under Newman these file rows are empty and the request fails with 400.

exec: pm.test("each missing field is named", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); ['present_address','permanent_address','country','state','city'].forEach(k => pm.expect(b).to.have.property(k)); });

request.description: **A seller logs in with phone number + password** (admins and buyers use email). A seller who cannot operate yet can **log in**, but may only use `/seller/me/...` (profile, password, resubmit). That is a seller still waiting (unverified / pending), a rejected seller, or an approved seller an admin has paused (status `inactive`). `can_operate` = verified **and** active. The response tells the app which screens to show: `verification_status`, `status`, `can_operate`. A **suspended** seller gets `401`.

exec: pm.test("not approved", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.can_operate).to.eql(false); pm.expect(b.status).to.eql('inactive'); pm.expect(b.verification_status).to.eql('unverified'); });

item.name: Seller Login — email no longer works (expect 400)

request.description: Sellers log in with **phone + password**. Sending an email instead is a `400` that asks for the phone.

exec: pm.test("asks for the phone", () => { pm.expect(pm.response.json().phone[0]).to.eql('This field is required.'); });

request.description: The same message is returned for a wrong password and for an unknown phone number, so nobody can find out which numbers are registered.

The seller's own profile: details, location, `business_info`, `media` (documents), `verification_status`, `verification_note` (the admin's reason when rejected), `status`, `is_seller_request`, `can_operate`. No password, wallet or change log.

exec: pm.test("has the NID from sign-up", () => { pm.expect(pm.response.json().media.map(m => m.media_for)).to.include('nid'); });
pm.test("no password or change log", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b).to.not.have.property('password'); pm.expect(b).to.not.have.property('profile_change_logs'); });

item.name: Edit my profile — name, address, skills

request.description: `PATCH` only the fields that change. Editable: name, photo (`profile_pic`), both addresses, country/state/city/thana, skills/education/experience/interest, the business profile (`info`) and documents. **Email and phone cannot be changed.** Every real change is written to the profile change log (admins read it on the seller detail).

exec: pm.test("saved", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.name).to.eql('Postman Applicant Renamed'); pm.expect(b.present_address).to.eql('New address, Feni'); });

item.name: Edit my profile — email cannot be changed (expect 400)

request.description: Sending the same email is fine; a different one is `400 {"email": ["Email cannot be changed."]}`.

item.name: Edit my profile — phone cannot be changed (expect 400)
Edit my profile — status and verification are ignored

request.description: A seller can never approve themselves. These fields are read-only; sending them changes nothing.

exec: pm.test("unchanged", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.status).to.eql('inactive'); pm.expect(b.verification_status).to.eql('unverified'); pm.expect(b.is_seller_request).to.eql(true); pm.expect(b.can_operate).to.eql(false); });

request.description: Send the whole business profile; the six business fields are required (`business_type`, `main_product`, `owner_name`, `employees_range`, `annual_revenue`, `established_year`). It is read back as `business_info`.

item.name: Edit my profile — upload a certificate

request.description: Documents are `media_for` + `media_file` pairs (multipart). `media_for`: `nid`, `birth_certificate`, `certificate`, `other`. JPG / PNG / WEBP / PDF, 5 MB each, 10 per request. **Pick a JPG, PNG, WEBP or PDF file for each `media_file` row in the Postman app** — a shared collection can't carry file paths, so under Newman these file rows are empty and the request fails with 400.

item.name: Edit my profile — delete the certificate

request.description: Remove a document by its `id` (from `media`). Replacing a document is a delete plus an upload in the same request.

item.name: Edit my profile — delete the only NID (expect 400)

request.description: At least one NID must always remain. To swap it, delete the old one and upload the new one in the same request.

The current password is required. The new one follows the password rules (8+ characters, not common, not all digits) and must differ from the current one. The token stays valid. The change is logged (the password itself is never stored in the log).

item.name: Log in with the new password

request.description: Only a **rejected** seller can resubmit. See the *approve, reject, resubmit* folder for the working call.

exec: pm.test("message", () => { pm.expect(pm.response.json().detail).to.eql('Only a rejected application can be resubmitted.'); });

item.name: Cannot operate yet: admin routes are still closed (expect 403)

request.description: A seller token never opens admin management, whatever the seller state.

item.name: Cannot operate yet: listings are closed (expect 403)

request.description: Listings need a seller who is verified **and** active. A seller who is still waiting, was rejected, or is paused only has the profile.
Approving takes two fields: `verification_status` (the KYC decision) and `status` (lets the seller log in). Send both in one request. Either one leaving its old value clears `is_seller_request`.

item.name: Approved seller — identity documents are locked (expect 400)

request.description: Once verified, NID and birth-certificate documents cannot be added or deleted by the seller (an admin can). Everything else stays editable. Other documents (certificates) are still fine. **Pick a JPG, PNG, WEBP or PDF file for each `media_file` row in the Postman app** — a shared collection can't carry file paths, so under Newman these file rows are empty and the request fails with 400.

exec: pm.test("tells them to ask an admin", () => { pm.expect(pm.response.json().media_for[0]).to.include('locked after verification'); });

item.name: Approved seller — can still edit the profile
[Admin step] Pause the approved seller (status inactive)

request.description: `inactive` pauses a seller: they can still log in and edit their profile, but nothing else, until an admin sets `active` again. This is separate from `verification_status` (an approved seller stays verified).

exec: pm.test("inactive, still verified", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.status).to.eql('inactive'); pm.expect(b.verification_status).to.eql('verified'); });

item.name: Paused seller (approved but inactive) can still log in

request.description: Approved (`verified`) but `inactive`: login still works, but this is now the **locked** tier, not profile-only — `can_operate` and `can_edit_profile` are both false.

exec: pm.test("verified but locked", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.verification_status).to.eql('verified'); pm.expect(b.status).to.eql('inactive'); pm.expect(b.can_operate).to.eql(false); pm.expect(b.can_edit_profile).to.eql(false); });

item.name: Paused seller CANNOT edit the profile (expect 403, locked)

request.description: verified + inactive is now the locked tier (an admin pausing an already-approved seller locks them out entirely, not just down to profile-only).
verified + inactive is locked, not profile-only: listings (and everything else outside GET /seller/me/) stay closed, same as before, but the message changed.

item.name: [Admin step] Make the seller active again
Seller listings (needs an approved, active seller)

request.description: Read-only lists for the listing form. Only **active** items are returned. `type` is `product` or `service`; `parent` filters a level of the tree; `search` matches the name.

exec: pm.test("only active product categories", () => { const r = pm.response.json().results; pm.expect(r.length).to.be.at.least(1); r.forEach(c => pm.expect(c.type).to.eql('product')); });
pm.test("service categories", () => { const r = pm.response.json().results; pm.expect(r.length).to.be.at.least(1); r.forEach(c => pm.expect(c.type).to.eql('service')); });

item.name: Lookup — attributes with their values (for SKU options)

exec: pm.test("attributes carry their values", () => { pm.response.json().results.forEach(a => pm.expect(a.values).to.be.an('array')); });

request.description: One endpoint for every product format (`listing_type`). Services are gigs: `/seller/gigs/`. The listing is **always `pending`** and owned by the seller. `seller`, `buyer`, `posted_by_role`, `status` and `requested_at` are not accepted. Required: `category`, `title`, `description`, and `skus` or `price` (`catalog_type` is always `product` here and optional). The Bangla fields (`title_bn`, `description_bn`, `condition_note_bn`, `warranty_bn`, `origin_bn`) are optional.

body.raw:
{
  "category": {{lk_category_id}},
  "catalog_type": "product",
  "listing_type": "general",
  "title": "{{listing_title}}",
  "title_bn": "পোস্টম্যান টি-শার্ট",
  "description": "Soft cotton t-shirt.",
  "description_bn": "নরম সুতির টি-শার্ট।",
  "origin": "Bangladesh",
  "origin_bn": "বাংলাদেশ",
  "price": "500",
  "discounted_price": "450",
  "stock_qty": 20,
  "status": "approved",
  "note": "ignored on create"
}

exec: pm.test("pending, with a request time", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.status).to.eql('pending'); pm.expect(b.requested_at).to.be.a('string'); });
pm.test("owner fields are not exposed", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); ['seller','buyer','posted_by_role','info_change_logs'].forEach(k => pm.expect(b).to.not.have.property(k)); });
pm.test("Bangla text saved", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.title_bn).to.eql('পোস্টম্যান টি-শার্ট'); pm.expect(b.origin_bn).to.eql('বাংলাদেশ'); });
pm.test("history starts with the seller", () => { const l = pm.response.json().status_change_logs; pm.expect(l.length).to.eql(1); pm.expect(l[0].creator_type).to.eql('seller'); });

request.description: A seller cannot have two listings with the same title (case and extra spaces do not matter). If the earlier listing was rejected, update that one instead.

exec: pm.test("tells the seller to update the existing one", () => { const m = pm.response.json().title[0]; pm.expect(m).to.include('You already have a listing with this title'); pm.expect(m).to.include('#' + pm.collectionVariables.get('listing_id')); });

item.name: Create a listing — a service (expect 400: it is a gig)

request.description: A seller's **services are gigs**: they are created on `/seller/gigs/` (see the **Seller gigs** folder). The product endpoint refuses `catalog_type: service`, the service-only fields (`delivery_days`, `urgent`, `package_includes`, ...) and the gig SKU fields (`price_type`, `duration`, `description`).

item.name: Create — no price and no SKU (expect 400)

request.description: Filters: `status`, `catalog_type`, `listing_type`, `category`, `brand`, `created_from` / `created_to`, `requested_from` / `requested_to`, `search` (title, Bangla title, SKU code, brand name), `ordering` (`created_at`, `updated_at`, `requested_at`, `title`, `status`, `id`), `limit`, `offset`.

exec: pm.test("wrapped list", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b).to.have.all.keys('count','next','previous','results'); pm.expect(b.count).to.be.at.least(1); });
pm.test("only pending, only mine, no owner fields", () => { pm.response.json().results.forEach(r => { pm.expect(r.status).to.eql('pending'); pm.expect(r).to.not.have.property('seller'); }); });

pm.test("only my product", () => { const r = pm.response.json().results; pm.expect(r.length).to.eql(1); pm.expect(String(r[0].id)).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('listing_id')); pm.expect(r[0].catalog_type).to.eql('product'); });

request.description: The full listing: SKUs with options, price tiers, media and the status history. The seller does not get the info change log.

exec: pm.test("full detail without the admin-only parts", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.skus.length).to.eql(1); pm.expect(b).to.not.have.property('info_change_logs'); pm.expect(b).to.not.have.property('seller'); });

pm.test("status history shows who, but not which admin", () => { pm.expect(Object.keys(pm.response.json().status_change_logs[0]).sort()).to.eql(['created_at','creator_type','id','note','status']); });

item.name: Edit a pending listing — stays pending

request.description: A seller can edit any of their listings. A pending listing stays pending and keeps its place in the admin's pending list.

item.name: Edit an APPROVED listing — it stays approved

request.description: Whatever a seller changes on an **approved** listing (content, SKUs, prices, stock), it **stays approved**. The change goes into the admin-only info change log. Prices and stock are changed through `skus` with the SKU `id`.

exec: pm.test("still approved", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.status).to.eql('approved'); pm.expect(b.price).to.eql('550.00'); });

item.name: A seller cannot set the status (expect it ignored)

exec: pm.test("unchanged", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.status).to.eql('approved'); pm.expect(b.note).to.eql(null); });

item.name: [Admin step] Reject the listing with a reason
The seller sees the rejection and the reason

exec: pm.test("rejected with the reason", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.status).to.eql('rejected'); pm.expect(b.note).to.eql('Please add a clear photo.'); });

item.name: Create with the rejected title (expect 400): update it instead

request.description: The title of a rejected listing is still taken. The seller must update that listing.

item.name: Save the rejected listing — this is the resubmit

request.description: There is **no Resubmit button**: any save by the seller on a `rejected` or `changes_requested` listing sends it back to `pending` and to the top of the admin's pending list (`requested_at` = now). The `note` sent now is the seller's message to the reviewer; the admin's reason stays in the history.

exec: pm.test("pending again, with the seller's message", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.status).to.eql('pending'); pm.expect(b.note).to.eql('Added a size chart.'); });

item.name: [Admin step] The pending list shows it first

request.description: Admin only. `status = pending`, newest request first, cursor pagination (`next` / `previous`, no `count`).

exec: pm.test("cursor shape", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b).to.have.property('next'); pm.expect(b).to.not.have.property('count'); });

item.name: [Admin step] Read the info change log

request.description: `info_change_logs` (admin only) lists every content change by the seller or an admin: `changed_fields`, and `previous_data` / `new_data` with the same keys. Stock is not recorded.

exec: pm.test("changes by the seller are logged", () => { const l = pm.response.json().info_change_logs; pm.expect(l.length).to.be.at.least(3); pm.expect(l.every(x => x.creator_type === 'seller')).to.eql(true); });

pm.test("the price change shows the SKU before and after", () => { const l = pm.response.json().info_change_logs.find(x => x.changed_fields.includes('skus')); pm.expect(l).to.exist; pm.expect(l.previous_data.skus[0].price).to.eql('500.00'); pm.expect(l.new_data.skus[0].price).to.eql('550.00'); pm.expect(l.previous_data.skus[0]).to.not.have.property('stock_qty'); });

item.name: Add files to my listing (POST, multipart)

request.description: A product or gig id of mine (`404` for anyone else's). `thumbnail` optional (`400` if one exists: use PATCH); `media_file` repeated, optional. Gallery limits for a seller: JPG, PNG, WEBP, GIF, MP4, PDF; 10 MB each, 10 per request, 20 per listing. **Select real files by hand in the Postman app** (a shared collection cannot carry file paths; under Newman the file parts are simply absent). Do not set Content-Type yourself.

item.name: Change files of my listing (PATCH, multipart)

request.description: Independent parts: a new `thumbnail` replaces the old; `remove_thumbnail=true` alone removes; `remove_media_ids` removes gallery files, `media_file` adds. It never changes the status. **Select real files by hand in the Postman app** (a shared collection cannot carry file paths; under Newman the file parts are simply absent). Do not set Content-Type yourself.

item.name: Remove the thumbnail of my listing
A gig id on the product endpoint (expect 404)

request.description: Products and gigs are separate endpoints: a gig is a 404 here (and a product id on `/seller/gigs/` is a 404).

item.name: A deleted listing is gone for the seller (expect 404)
Seller gigs (needs an approved, active seller)

request.description: A **gig** is a service the seller offers. It is created on `/seller/gigs/`: always `pending`, owned by the seller (`seller`, `buyer`, `posted_by_role`, `status`, `requested_at` are ignored). It is priced by **packages**: one SKU per `price_type` (`hourly`, `daily`, `weekly`, `monthly`, `fixed`), `price` is the rate for that unit. A package has no duration: the buyer chooses it when ordering and pays the rate times it. No options, stock, brand or quantity prices. For one package send `price` and `price_type` on the gig instead of `skus`.

exec: const g = pm.response.json(); pm.collectionVariables.set('gig_id', String(g.id)); pm.collectionVariables.set('gig_sku_id', String(g.skus.find(s => s.price_type === 'hourly').id));
pm.test('pending, with a request time', () => { pm.expect(g.status).to.eql('pending'); pm.expect(g.requested_at).to.be.a('string'); });
pm.test('owner fields are not exposed', () => ['seller','buyer','posted_by_role','info_change_logs'].forEach(k => pm.expect(g).to.not.have.property(k)));

pm.test('two packages, no duration on a SKU', () => { pm.expect(g.skus.length).to.eql(2); const h = g.skus.find(s => s.price_type === 'hourly'); pm.expect(h.price).to.eql('400.00'); pm.expect(h).to.not.have.property('duration'); });
pm.test('no stock, no options', () => g.skus.forEach(s => { pm.expect(s.stock_qty).to.eql(null); pm.expect(s.variants).to.eql([]); }));
pm.test('history starts with the seller', () => { const l = g.status_change_logs; pm.expect(l.length).to.eql(1); pm.expect(l[0].creator_type).to.eql('seller'); });

item.name: Create a gig — the same title again (expect 400)

request.description: One live gig per title for a seller (case and extra spaces ignored); update the existing gig instead. A product with the same title is allowed.

exec: pm.test('tells the seller to update it', () => pm.expect(JSON.stringify(pm.response.json())).to.include('already have a listing with this title'));

item.name: Create a gig — a package without a price type (expect 400)

request.description: `price_type` is required on every gig package.

item.name: Create a gig — two packages with one price type (expect 400)

request.description: A gig has at most one package per price type.

item.name: Create a gig — stock on a gig (expect 400)

request.description: A gig has no stock.

item.name: Create a gig — a product-only field (expect 400)

request.description: Brand, model, origin, warranty, measurement, condition, quantity prices, ... are for products.

item.name: My gigs — filter by status and price type

request.description: Filters: `status`, `category`, `price_type`, `created_*`, `requested_*`, `search`, `ordering`. Rows carry `price_type` of the lowest rate and `image_url`.

exec: pm.test('only my gig', () => { const r = pm.response.json().results; pm.expect(r.length).to.eql(1); pm.expect(String(r[0].id)).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('gig_id')); pm.expect(r[0].price_type).to.eql('hourly'); });

request.description: Packages, media, thumbnail and the status history (not the info change log).

item.name: A product id on the gig endpoint (expect 404)
Edit a pending gig — stays pending

request.description: Gigs are moderated on `/catalog/gigs/` (their own pending list: `/catalog/gigs/requests/`).

item.name: Edit an APPROVED gig (change a package) — it stays approved

request.description: An approved gig stays approved whatever the seller changes; the admin sees it in the info change log. Packages merge by `id`; they are hidden with `is_active: false`, never deleted.

exec: pm.test('approved, new rate', () => { const g = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(g.status).to.eql('approved'); const h = g.skus.find(s => String(s.id) === pm.collectionVariables.get('gig_sku_id')); pm.expect(h.price).to.eql('450.00'); });

request.description: One package per price type.

item.name: [Admin step] Reject the gig with a reason
The seller sees the rejection and the reason

exec: pm.test('rejected with the reason', () => { const g = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(g.status).to.eql('rejected'); pm.expect(g.note).to.eql('Please add a clear thumbnail.'); });

item.name: Change the gig files (multipart) — the status does not change

request.description: Rejected sellers log in and keep can_edit_profile=true (a deliberate carve-out — status is suspended for a rejected seller, but they still need to fix their profile/documents and resubmit).

exec: pm.test("rejected, suspended, but still profile-editable (carve-out)", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.verification_status).to.eql('rejected'); pm.expect(b.status).to.eql('suspended'); pm.expect(b.can_operate).to.eql(false); pm.expect(b.can_edit_profile).to.eql(true); });

request.description: Documents can be swapped too: delete the old NID and upload the new one in the same request (the seller is not verified, so identity documents are not locked).

Moves a **rejected** seller to `pending`, puts them back in the admin's Seller Request queue (`is_seller_request: true`, `requested_at` = now) and adds a history entry made by the seller. The optional `note` is the seller's message to the reviewer; the old rejection reason stays in `verification_logs`.

exec: pm.test("pending, back in the queue, not approved, still profile-editable", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.verification_status).to.eql('pending'); pm.expect(b.is_seller_request).to.eql(true); pm.expect(b.can_operate).to.eql(false); pm.expect(b.status).to.eql('inactive'); pm.expect(b.can_edit_profile).to.eql(true); });
pm.test("note is the seller's message", () => { pm.expect(pm.response.json().verification_note).to.eql('Replaced the NID with a clear scan'); });
